context_documents.title: 2023-930 · A borrowed belt gripper needs its operating clearance, not just its layout
context_documents.body:
# 2023-930: A borrowed belt gripper needs its operating clearance, not just its layout

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The polyurethane-belt gripper credits WildStang’s published work. Stand-offs keep running belts away from the carpet. A continuously rigged, internally belted elevator leaves an open arm passage; an auxiliary cube collector is discussed as a later low/link opportunity.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team cites grip on cones, carpet protection and keeping elevator gearing/mass low. The auxiliary collector must remain a proposal unless its later fielded configuration is established.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Copying the contact belt without its stand-offs can create both carpet damage and an unintended ground reaction on the arm. A low-mounted drive reduces moving mass, while an open passage permits acquisition on the opposite side. The strategic value of an added cube collector depends on finishing links quickly, not simply acquiring another mechanism.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test floor clearance under chassis pitch, compare both piece types, and measure complete low-node cycles before adding the proposed subsystem.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/wzWFWZzy9C8](https://youtu.be/wzWFWZzy9C8)

source_reviews.title: 930 CAD and code release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read release and the complete elevator routing reply.
source_reviews.facts: Team describes standard continuous belt rigging, two bolted aluminum tubes in the first stage, belt ends attached to top and bottom of the carriage, and an internal belt route chosen for packaging and protection.
source_reviews.limitations: Linked CAD and Java were not inspected. Diagram is identified in the text, with no visual measurements taken.

source_reviews.title: 930 interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.
source_reviews.facts: Older record describes a pass-through arm, polyurethane belt gripper and an auxiliary low cube collector proposed at filming.
source_reviews.limitations: Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional.

source_reviews.title: 930 CommandFactoryUtility.java
source_reviews.locator: Ground-intake extend and retract command factories, lines 334–398, blob 87a91f3ca80aa39cbdbbd5e2082f202b64113a2b
source_reviews.facts: Ground-intake factory starts the manipulator roller, extends the collector, commands the elevator and arm toward pickup, waits on manipulator current, then stows the arm before retracting the intake.
source_reviews.limitations: Static read. Timing and current criteria do not prove a physical transfer or event installation.

source_reviews.title: 930 RobotContainer.java
source_reviews.facts: Active bindings include reverse cube pickup with the arm and a separate driver trigger for the ground intake extend/retract command factories.
source_reviews.limitations: Release branch includes software support. Event installation and mechanism purpose by match are unresolved.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Team 930's CAD release directly documents the lift's continuous belt and its protected route. The older interview account explains how that lift fits into the scoring machine. An arm moves through the opening between the structural members while carrying a piece in a belt-based tool. The layout gives the tool access to useful approach directions while the stage structure remains tall enough to serve the grid.
piece_flow: Acquire into the gripper and retain the piece in the same tool. The older synopsis describes polyurethane belts and stand-offs to keep the belts clear of carpet.
Move the arm and carriage through a collision-free sequence. Pass-through gives a potential route to the other side while keeping the original grip.
Release at the selected node and retract. The proposed auxiliary cube intake in the interview is a separate route whose deployment status remains unresolved.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The two bolted tubes support and enclose a useful routing volume. Internal belt runs protect the transmission from contact and free external clearance, but hidden belt edges and anchors must remain inspectable. The pass-through opening has to clear the carried piece, not just the arm CAD. Grid, bumper, elevator and wrist also bound how much directional flexibility the drive team can actually use.

subsystems.name: Continuously rigged elevator
subsystems.construction: Team describes a belt routed inside aluminum tubes, with its ends connected to the top and bottom of the carriage.
subsystems.operation: Belt motion controls carriage position while the rail stack supports the scoring arm.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team states packaging and protection as reasons for internal routing.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Internal routing can make a belt serviceable only if there is a path to fish, tension and anchor a replacement with the arm installed. The bolted stage can also accumulate alignment error.
subsystems.interfaces: The elevator sets arm height and carries bending and torsional load when the gripper extends or reverses.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect tube-edge clearance and belt tracking through the entire stroke. Time belt replacement before assuming internal routing improves service.
subsystems.unknowns: Belt pitch, detailed pulley geometry, tension settings and loaded deflection.

subsystems.name: Pass-through arm and gripper
subsystems.construction: Carbon-fiber arm and belt-based gripper are from the older interview. The belt elevator is a distinct subsystem.
subsystems.operation: Carry the retained piece through the arm's working envelope and release from a selected direction.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older account attributes stand-offs to keeping intake belts off carpet.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Reducing arm mass can improve motion at the expense of sensitivity to joint attachment and impact. Check the complete loaded envelope and end-tool sag after reversal.
subsystems.interfaces: Pickup height depends on wrist angle and stand-off position. The lift opening limits allowable piece yaw during reversal.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check bonded or fastened interfaces using actual construction details when available. Inspect worn belts and floor stand-offs after a hard landing.
subsystems.unknowns: Tube layup, joint attachments, compression and capture envelope.

subsystems.name: Preset and auxiliary route
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes the proposed auxiliary route. Released code declares an intake extension motor, roller motor and a driver binding for the ground intake sequence.
subsystems.operation: The code positions the elevator and arm for intake after collector extension, uses manipulator current in the sequence, then stows the arm before collector retraction.
subsystems.team_rationale: The auxiliary route's link value is an engineering interpretation of the older account.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Time the actual low-link cycle and compare with the main arm before assigning the volume, wiring and driver inputs to a second mechanism.
subsystems.interfaces: A low intake can occupy the arm's collection sweep and change the possession logic.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Exercise wrong preset and delayed retraction scenarios before integrating an auxiliary path.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual competition installation and whether the proposed direct low-scoring function was fielded.

revisions: Older interview reports aluminum-to-carbon-fiber arm evolution and presents the low route as future work at filming. June release and July reply establish publication dates only.
transferable_principles: For a pass-through lift, route protected drive elements and harnesses outside the volume occupied by the retained piece.
disconfirming_conditions: The layout loses value if piece or harness clearance forces a stop-and-regrip, or if the alternate route rarely saves a chassis turn.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, release branch deployment by event, and mechanical validation of the auxiliary intake. FIRST records Benedict Cargohub while the older dossier uses Cubert Conelius. The team number and season identify the record.
recommended_images: Use the original belt-path diagram linked in post 3 and obtain a source-linked loaded pass-through view.
